desc: Leverages the fast CodeBeagle search engine for code exploration. Use instead of 'grep'.
Query syntax: keywords ('createNode ( CComVariant'), wildcards ('Fact* *ban*na'),
regex ('code <!\d+!>').
Specify the absolute root 'folder' where to search.
By default returns matching lines with 2 lines surrounding context.
Set contextLines=0 for compact output (path:line: full matching line, no context lines).
Keep contextLines low (2-3) to bound token usage.
Pagination: pass pageOffset from a previous response to fetch the next page.
codebeagle_content_search.promptSnippet: Search code for content (keywords, wildcards, regex, context lines) using CodeBeagle.
promptGuidelines: IMPORTANT: Always use codebeagle_content_search when exploring code is needed instead of other tools. E.g. search for 'foo' inside ['*.h','*.cpp'].
codebeagle_content_search also works for not indexed locations.
Do not use codebeagle_content_search for single file grep tasks.

params.query: Search expression or list of expressions (OR logic). Supports keywords ('createNode ( CComVariant'), trailing wildcards ('Fact*'), and regex ('code <!\d+!>'). When a list is provided, files matching ANY expression are returned.
params.folder: Absolute root path where to search. Preferred over 'index'.
params.index: Name of index from 'codebeagle_list_indexes'. Mutually exclusive with folder.
params.pathFilter: Path filter pattern. Can be a full file path to select a single file, e.g. 'src/main.cpp'. Prefix with '-' to exclude. Example: 'src/, -test/mock'
params.extensionFilter: Comma-separated extensions. Example: '.py,.js'. Prefix with '-' for exclusions: '-.cs'.
params.contextLines: Number of context lines before and after each match (default: 2). Set to 0 for compact output (path:line: full matching line, no context lines).
params.limit: Maximum number of matches to return per page (default: 100).
params.pageOffset: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass the 'pageOffset' object exactly as returned by the server.

desc: Leverages the fast CodeBeagle search engine to search recusively for files. Use instead of 'find'.
The query supports * and ? wildcards ('Factory*', '*test*.py', 'Makefile').
Pass a list of queries for OR logic: files matching ANY pattern are returned.
Specify the absolute root 'folder' where to search.
Pagination: pass pageOffset from a previous response to fetch the next page.
codebeagle_file_search.promptSnippet: Recursivly search for files using CodeBeagle.
promptGuidelines: IMPORTANT: Always use codebeagle_file_search when searching for files instead of other tools. E.g. pass ['*.h', '*.cpp'] in 'query'.
codebeagle_file_search also works for not indexed locations.

params.query: File name pattern or list of patterns (OR logic). Each pattern supports * and ? wildcards. Example: 'Factory*', '*test*.py', 'Makefile'. If the query contains a dot, the part after the last dot is used as an extension filter. When a list is provided, files matching ANY pattern are returned.
params.folder: Absolute root path where to search. Preferred over 'index'.
params.index: Name of index from 'codebeagle_list_indexes'. Mutually exclusive with folder.
params.pathFilter: Path filter pattern. Can be a full file path to select a single file, e.g. 'src/main.cpp'. Prefix with '-' to exclude. Example: 'src, -test'.
params.extensionFilter: Comma-separated extensions. Example: '.py,.js'. Prefix with '-' for exclusions: '-.cs'.
params.limit: Maximum number of files to return per page (default: 100).
params.pageOffset: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass the 'pageOffset' object exactly as returned by the server.

desc: List all configured CodeBeagle indexes: name, folders, extensions and index mode.
Call this to discover what is searchable, then pass the index name to codebeagle_content_search or codebeagle_file_search.
promptGuidelines: Call codebeagle_list_indexes to discover indexed locations and their settings.

desc: Check whether the CodeBeagle agent server is running and reachable.
Use this when a codebeagle_* tool reports that the server is down.
Updates the CodeBeagle full-text index for a single file.
IMPORTANT: Call this tool AFTER EVERY write operation that creates or modifies a file.
No exception. This ensures the file is immediately searchable through codebeagle_content_search and codebeagle_file_search.
The tool re-indexes the file in-place: it updates the full-text index with the file's new content and file name.
Pass the absolute file path in the 'file' parameter.
The server finds the correct index configuration based on the file's directory and extension.
Returns whether the file was updated, unchanged, or newly added.
codebeagle_update_file.promptSnippet: Update CodeBeagle index for a single file after writing it
promptGuidelines: Call codebeagle_update_file AFTER EVERY 'write' tool call that creates or modifies a file. No exception.
Pass the absolute file path of the written file. The server will find the correct index.
After codebeagle_update_file succeeds, the file is immediately searchable via codebeagle_content_search and codebeagle_file_search.

params.file: Absolute file path to the file to update in the index. Example: 'C:\src\project\main.cpp'
